text: The slot holds the head `discriminant` for `tinyclip-39m-16` (shrinkage 0.03), fitted on `images/alachua-pre2025 (licence rule nc)`, with 5391 species rows, and a bias a row. Every photo's vector (`images/alachua-2025.wasm-int8-per-channel`) went through `tools/fusion/fuse.py`, the reference of the page's arithmetic, with the slot's own files as the page reads them (half-precision rows). Settings: rule `mix`, t_kind 0.5, w_kind 0.7, alpha_prior 0.75. On 1803 tuning photos (val) the thresholds came out as name_at 0.89 and offer_at 0.98. On the 4197 test photos the kind of eye is right for 89.1% (88.2 to 90.1); the top species is right for 53.8% (52.2 to 55.4) and is among the first five for 75.1% (73.8 to 76.5). `person` was said for 0.00% of these photos and `none` for 0.00%; the set holds neither. The top species from fuse.py differs from a direct matrix computation on the same files for 0 photos. The kinds head is `kind rows fitted on the fitting photos and the extra set (a kind's photos weighted by the inverse square root of their number)`. With kind_at 0.53 (set on wildlife tuning photos and the extra set's tuning third), the page asserts a kind for 81.7% (80.6 to 82.9) of the wildlife test photos and is right for 96.3% (95.7 to 96.9) of those; for the 18.3% (17.1 to 19.4) where it is not sure, the true kind is among its three likeliest for 89.5% (87.2 to 91.5). On the 1240 test photos of people, cats, dogs, grazing animals and rooms (`images/coco-kinds.wasm-int8-per-channel`), the kind is right for 96.9% (95.8 to 97.8); the page asserts a kind for 95.2% (94.0 to 96.4) and is right for 98.4% (97.6 to 99.1) of those; where it is not sure the true kind is among its three likeliest for 96.7% (91.7 to 100.0). A species is named on 15.1% (13.1 to 17.1) of these photos. The slot needs: species.bias_url (build 7 of the page); kinds.bias (build 7 of the page); fusion.rule mix (build 7 of the page); fusion.kind_at (the build of the page that has the answer `not sure`).
